FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Engineering Division Mine Sectional Committee had been approved by the Heavy Mechanical Council. This standard industry. is prepared to harmonizing the graphical symbols for use on mine plans in mining

Symbols and graphical representations are used to convey instructions and messages at a glance and cosidere d to be quick methods of communicant ion. Any ambiguity or misinterpretation of a symbol may lead to problem. Therefore symbols should be devised with utmost care to convey what exactly is to be conveyed. The symbols may have to be devised for use at national of use. level or company level or for specific area/field

IS 13230:1992

Indian Standard

GRAPHICAL SYMBOLS FOR USE ON MINE PLANS
1SCOPE This standard lays down the graphical symbols for use on mine plans required to be maintained by mine management under statutory requirements. 2 REFERENCES

3 RULES OF PRESENTATION 3.1 Classification For ease of utilisation, classified into two groups: symbols have been

4 SIZE OF MINE PLANS The mine plans shall be prepared on drawing sheets of sizes specified for A-series of IS 1064 : 1961. For other aspects of drawing such as layout, numbering and referencing of sheets etc. the recommendations made by IS 696 : 1972 shall be followed as far as practicable. 5 SCALES For preparation of various mine plans, of following scales is recommended: the use

a) Symbo!s for coal mines; and b) Symbols for metalliferous 3.1'.1 Individual mines.

symbols are specified in 6.

3.2 Size of Symbols Size of symbols shall vary proportionately according to the scale used for the plan. In this standard, the size has been specified for the scale of 1 : 2 000. 3.3 Size of Letters Letters used in the preparation of the mine plan shall be of 20, 14, 10, 7, 5, 3, and 2 mm size. Letters shall be written in the capital letters ( except for standard abbreviation for units ) for clear and easy comprehension on drawings.

1 : 200, 1 : 500, 1 : 1 000, 1 : 2 000, 1 : 5 000, 1 : 10 000, 1 : 20 000, 1 : 50 000, 1 : 100 000. 6 SYMBOLS Symbols for coal mines and metalliferous mines are given in column 3 Table 1 and Table 2 respectively. Column 4 of Table 1 and Table 2 indicate the colour schemes and other additional information, if any, of these symbols.

is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system o inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated, by the producer. Standard parked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard asla further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS.
